steps.headline: Every provider is now one row shape: name, a grey status line, one button. The Default engine badge is gone.
steps.changed: Your note on P-1. Claude Code, ChatGPT and OpenRouter share one row: the name, a one-line status in the same grey, one button on the right (Preferences, Sign in with ChatGPT, Connect to OpenRouter). Claude Code's Default engine title and its sentence are removed; the (i) beside the heading still says sessions run through Claude Code unless another provider is picked.
steps.notice: No green text anywhere in the window. Signed in reads as words in the status line, like the Account row does.
steps.risk: Nothing on the row says Claude Code is the default any more; only the (i) and the opening sentence do.

steps.path: Settings → Model Providers, both plans signed in
steps.headline: Signed in, a plan's row carries the same two bars the usage card draws: 5-hour limit and 7-day limit, with reset times.
steps.changed: Your note on P-2. The signed-in line is plain grey: Signed in as your email, with the plan name (ChatGPT Plus) under it. Beneath, the 5-hour and 7-day bars, exactly as the /usage card draws them, coloured by how full they are. The Claude Code row gets the same bars for the Claude plan, so both plans read the same way.
steps.notice: Sign out is an outlined button on the right, where Preferences and Connect sit on the other rows.
steps.risk: Two sets of bars make the window taller; OpenRouter and Local Models sit one scroll further down.

steps.path: Settings → Model Providers → ChatGPT, mid sign-in
steps.headline: Waiting is one short line with a spinner, and a Cancel. The extra sentence under it is gone.
steps.changed: Your note on P-3. The status reads Waiting for the browser… beside a small spinner; Cancel on the right. Nothing else under the row.
steps.notice: Cancel puts the row back to Not signed in.
steps.risk: There is no longer a line saying which tab to look in; the browser tab that opened is the only cue.

steps.path: Settings → Model Providers → ChatGPT, when OpenAI refuses
steps.headline: When OpenAI refuses the account, the status stays grey and OpenAI's reason sits on its own red line beneath it.
steps.changed: Your note on P-4. Signed in as your email in the normal grey; OpenAI's reason (for example, a workspace admin turning it off) on a second line in the destructive colour; Sign out on the right. No bars, because there is no plan to draw.
steps.notice: The reason is OpenAI's own text, not ours.
steps.risk: A long reason wraps to two lines and pushes the rows below down.

steps.headline: Three sign-ins stacked full width: Claude filled, ChatGPT and OpenRouter outlined. The link reads Use an API key or local model.
steps.changed: Your note on P-5. Log in with OpenRouter joins the card. Its sign-in is the browser round-trip in the 2026-08-31 OpenRouter spec, which is written but not built, so the button is real and its backend is on the to-do list. The sentence above reads Sign in with the plan you already pay for. The link under the buttons is now Use an API key or local model.
steps.notice: The link still opens the key box it opened before; a local-model route on this screen needs its own step later, and is noted as such.
steps.risk: Three tall buttons make the card taller; on a short window the link sits near the bottom edge.

steps.headline: While the browser is open the card stays, with the waiting line inside it. The Skip setup link is gone.
steps.changed: Your note on P-6. The same framed card holds the spinner and A browser window should have opened. Finish signing in to ChatGPT there… — the screen no longer changes shape. The Skip setup (I installed via terminal) link at the bottom is removed on every step of the wizard.
steps.notice: Someone who installed Claude Code by hand now signs in like everyone else; there is no way past this screen without a sign-in or a key.
steps.risk: That is a real change for terminal installs: the old skip let them into the app without signing in here.

steps.path: A ChatGPT conversation when the plan's window is used up
steps.headline: The used-up-plan card is one bubble: the message, what the other provider costs, and a single Switch button.
steps.changed: Your note on P-9. One red-ringed bubble, like the other stop cards: Your ChatGPT plan's 5-hour limit is used up. It resets at 6:43 PM. Then, in grey inside the same sentence, Claude Sonnet 4.6 on OpenRouter is connected and bills per use. A small Switch button at the right edge of the bubble. The separate button row under the bubble is gone.
steps.notice: Switch rebinds this conversation to that model; the status-bar chip changes. With nothing else connected, the bubble is the message alone.
steps.risk: On a narrow window the sentence wraps to two lines before the button; that is how the stalled card already behaves.

steps.path: Status bar → model chip → search gpt
steps.headline: The plan's models are grouped under ChatGPT Plan, as you asked.
steps.changed: Your note on P-10. The provider is labelled ChatGPT Plan in the picker's rows and its group; the Settings section heading stays ChatGPT.
steps.notice: The status-bar chip's provider name follows the same label.
steps.risk: None beyond the wider label in the picker row.
